Q: Git debugging - "error: could not delete references: cannot lock ref" "File exists" A:

I had the same problem when doing git fetch -apt, and my issue is the one tracked in (still open):

  • https://github.com/git-for-windows/git/issues/5378
  • https://github.com/git-for-windows/git/issues/5900

Considered that re-cloning is safer than manipulating .git folder internals, you can still proceed with the following solution that worked for me on windows; it's an hard reset the pack-refs:

  1. Make sure everything is committed or stashed.

  2. Remove all the packed-refs folder:

    Remove-Item .git\packed-refs -Force

  3. Re-fetch and rebuild the references:

    git fetch --all --prune
git pack-refs --all

  4. Move into the correct branch where you want to be:

    git switch main

  5. Verify everything is correct:

    git fsck --full --strict

  6. If you want to clean up everything and clean dangling commits normalize everything use:

    git gc --prune=now

After step 6 the fsck command said everything was perfect for me.
Still, remember that re-cloning is the safest option if you're unsure.

Q: Fencing in old C++ compilers A:

I want a variable to behave atomically

Atomicity applies to loads, stores, compare-and-swap and some read-modify-write operations for a subset of built-in types. E.g. CPUs provide atomic add/sub read-modify-write instructions, but no atomic negate/multiply/divide.

Read-modify-write instructions are efficient but optional hardware optimizations for what otherwise requires a loop with an atomic load, non-atomic modify, and atomic compare-and-swap store, which retries when comparison finds that the object has been modified by another thread since the load in this thread.

Which operations on your variable need to behave atomically?

Is there any other way to achieve atomicity under these conditions

Another option is using pre-C++11 compiler built-in functions for atomic memory access:

https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc-4.4.7/gcc/Atomic-Builtins.html#Atomic-Builtins

These compiler built-in functions for atomic compare-and-swap and read-modify-write operations made possible implementing POSIX mutex in the C standard library in portable fashion without leaking any implementation details into user's code.

Atomic compare-and-swap is required for implementing mutex lock/unlock operations, otherwise impossible with only atomic loads and stores alone.

Q: Multi-page form validation issue with react-hook-form and arrays A:

Solution

You should be using separate forms for each page and collect all the different forms' data using either a 3rd party library for this or some custom-defined higher state. This is the recommended approach by the official react-hook-form docs, see Advanced Usage > Wizard Form / Funnel.

Explanation of the problem itself

The problem you're having is that when you click "Next", it invokes handleSubmit which validates the data prior to invoking the onSubmit callback (see docs).

This is not a problem when you first load the page with PageOne, as it includes only a required input field that you populate prior to clicking "Next" for the first time, but it becomes a problem once PageTwo loads - it adds a required items field to the form which is invalid by default until you add an actual item to it.

You should only ever use handleSubmit if you intend to validate and submit all of the form data; you should not use it to open/load another part of the same form (emphasis on "same").
